attempts.name: settings-ui-automation-125-live-proof
attempts.mechanism: same UIAutomation path at a supported step

attempts.name: ccd-dpi-scale-150
attempts.blocker: The display source reports maxRelativeScale=1 (recommended + 1 = 125% maximum). The 150% step requires relative +2, beyond the source's supported range, so the OS cannot apply 150% on this panel.

attempts.name: registry-logpixels-broadcast-150
attempts.mechanism: HKCU\Control Panel\Desktop LogPixels=144 + Win8DpiScaling=1 + SendMessageTimeout(HWND_BROADCAST, WM_SETTINGCHANGE, 'Display'/'WindowMetrics')

settingsOptionObservation.method: UI Automation on SystemSettings_Display_Scaling_ItemSizeOverride_ComboBox (successful enumeration earlier in this session)
settingsOptionObservation.note: The WinUI Settings ComboBox popup is not reliably enumerable on every attempt (later runs returned no popup items); the CCD supported-range query below is the authoritative evidence.

blockers: Settings UI Automation: 150% is not selectable. The successful scale-option enumeration in this session exposed only ["100% (Recommended)", "125%"]; the explicit 150% selection attempt returned scale-item-not-found (output recorded above). Later UIA attempts could not enumerate the WinUI popup reliably, so the CCD query below is treated as authoritative.

CCD API: display source reports minRelativeScale=0, curRelativeScale=0, maxRelativeScale=1 (recommended + 1 = 125% maximum supported). DisplayConfigSetDeviceInfo for the 150% step (relative +2) returned success (setErr=0) and GET then reported curRelative=2, BUT the measured live Electron scale factor became 1.3125 (ratio 1.250 vs baseline), i.e. 125% — Windows clamped the applied live scale to the supported maximum, not 150%. A supported-step set (relative +1) DID apply live: scaleFactor 1.0499999523162842 -> 1.3125.
Registry+broadcast: LogPixels=144 + Win8DpiScaling=1 + WM_SETTINGCHANGE did not change the measured live scale factor (1.0499999523162842 -> 1.0499999523162842). Registry DPI is applied at sign-in.

Host display is a single 1366x768 source; Windows hides/refuses scale steps that would reduce the effective desktop below its minimum supported size (150% => ~911x512 DIP), consistent with the Settings list and CCD maxRelativeScale.
